# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 19 (Bu-Vb Pc19)

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 19. Applying excessive materials to a large dwelling

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahallakavihāra-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 19; Vin IV 47) is a training rule governing the construction of large monastic residences (*mahallaka vihāra*) [Roth 1997; Tan 2002; SuttaCentral]. According to the origin story (*nidāna*), the rule was occasioned by the obstinate monk Channa, who, while gathering sticks and grass to construct his lodging, damaged a brāhmaṇa's cornfield [Tan 2002; Tan 2004, 2008]. The rule stipulates that a monk who applies more than three layers of building materials when roofing or plastering a large dwelling commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In monastic terminology, a *mahallaka vihāra* stands in contrast to a smaller hut or dwelling (*khuddaka vihāra*) [Roth 1997]. Although situated within the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, this regulation is classified as applying equally to both monks and nuns (*sādhāraṇa-paññatti*), corresponding to Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 115 [Hüsken 1997; SuttaCentral].

The rule is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing as Pācittiya 19 or 20 in the Prātimokṣas and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [Roth 1997; SuttaCentral]. Automated text alignment via DharmaNexus corroborates these cross-language relationships, identifying correspondences in the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3), *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), and *Prātimokṣasūtra* commentaries [DharmaNexus]. Internally, the text shares significant technical phrasing with the Khandhaka sections on dwellings and building work—most notably the *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16) and *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15)—as well as the Saṅghādisesa rules on construction (Ss 5 and Ss 7) [DharmaNexus].
